summary: Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the Australian National University and earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He has served as an Associate Professor at the University of Sydney since 2002.

Mark Collins worked in linguistics and Indology, earning degrees at the University of London and the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Karl Brugmann, and Bruno Lindner. His appointments included professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Trinity College, Hartford, and the University of Madras.

Mark Condos is a historian of India and imperial history who completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge (2009–2013). He held a fellowship at Queen Mary University of London in 2014 and became Senior Lecturer at King's College London in 2020.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He served as an Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1994–2006) and became a Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 2010.

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford and completed his PhD at the University of Exeter (1988–1990). He lectured at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) before serving as Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a historian specializing in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University in ~2003.
Mark Hale is a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. His academic career includes attested posts at Harvard University in 1987 and Concordia University in 1997.

Mark I. Wallace is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Paul Ricœur at the University of Chicago (PhD ~1982–1986). After teaching at Georgia State University (~1987–1989), he became Professor of Religion at Swarthmore College in ~1989.

Mark Jan Dresden worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguistics, completing his PhD at Utrecht under Jan Gonda and studying at Cambridge. He was Professor of Iranian Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1980) and President of the American Oriental Society (1973–1974).

Mark Juergensmeyer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1967–1974). In 1993, he became Director of Global and International Studies and professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held appointments at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2004–2006) and is attested in 2026 as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair in Japanese Studies at the University of California, Berkeley.

Mark McClish is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Patrick Olivelle. His academic career includes an attested post at Birmingham-Southern College in 2012.
Mark Owen is an academic working in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Pedersen is a scholar in computational linguistics who earned his PhD from the University of Queensland by 2001 and subsequently held a post at the same institution.

Mark Rowe is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. His career includes an appointment at McMaster University, where he is attested from 2015 and as Associate Professor of Religious Studies in 2026.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski was an Indologist who earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University and a PhD at the University of Oxford (~1975–1979) under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, alongside traditional study under Swami Lakshman Joo and others.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught at Illinois State University (~1979–2008), where he became Emeritus Professor of Philosophy in ~2008, before serving as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Seoul National University (~2008–2012).

Mark Singleton specializes in Indology and religious studies, completing an M.Phil and PhD at the University of Cambridge (2003–2006) under Elizabeth De Michelis. He served as Professor at St John's College (2007–2013) and Senior Research Fellow at SOAS in 2015.

Mark T. Unno specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, having studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University. He held a post at Brown University (~1994–1998) before joining the University of Oregon in ~1998 as Assistant Professor of East Asian Religions.

Mark Tatz was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz while also studying under traditional Tibetan teachers. He served as a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).
